info.title: TikTak.by MCP Analytics API
info.description:
Read-only analytics API powering the local MCP server (tiktak-mcp). All endpoints return a `{query, data, meta}` envelope. All amounts are in BYN.

## Methodology (locked 2026-05-14)

Numbers reproduce the legacy admin reports /bb/reports.php, /bb/sales_breakdown.php, /bb/dohrash2.php, /bb/cat_analysis.php:

- **Revenue** = SUM(r_paid + delivery_paid) over UNION(rent_sub_deals_act, rent_sub_deals_arch), filtered by `acc_date` (accounting date — when the payment landed). Not by parent deal's `cr_time`.
- **Deal/return counts** read UNION(rent_deals_act, rent_deals_arch). The `_act` table holds ~430 currently-open deals; querying only `_arch` would miss them.
- **Office attribution** uses sub_deal.place + delivery_yn (per-payment), not deal.first_rent_place (per-deal). A deal opened at office 1 but extended at office 2 contributes to BOTH.
- **Carnival** items are detected via tovar_rent_cat.cat_type=1. Numeric endpoints accept `include_carnival` (default true). When include_carnival=true /finance/pnl still splits revenue into revenue_carnival_byn / revenue_non_carnival_byn.
- **Inventory** at date X counts both tovar_rent_items (buy_date <= X) and tovar_rent_items_arch (buy_date <= X AND arch_time >= X) — matches tovar::getTovNumberForCatsForDate.
- **/inventory/utilization** denominator uses average of unit counts at period start and end.

## Notes on amount serialization

Amount fields suffixed `_byn` are returned either as JSON numbers or as decimal strings, depending on the endpoint:
- Endpoints that compute the amount in PHP (e.g. /finance/pnl rolls up expense buckets and casts to float) return numbers.
- Endpoints that pass MariaDB ROUND(..., 2) results straight through (DECIMAL columns) return JSON strings such as `"424231.72"`. Always parse `_byn` fields as numeric.

Access: Bearer token (MCP_API_TOKEN), GeoIP-restricted to BY/RU, rate-limited to 60 req/min.

from.name: from
from.description: Period start (ISO date). Default: 12 months ago.

category.name: category
category.description: Single category slug, or comma-separated list/array of slugs (e.g. 'children,medical'). Default: 'all'.

location.name: location
location.description: Office id (1..) for non-courier sub-deals (sub_deal.place=N AND delivery_yn != '1'), 'courier' for delivery_yn='1', or 'all'.

include_carnival.name: include_carnival
include_carnival.description: If false, exclude items in carnival categories (tovar_rent_cat.cat_type=1). Truthy/falsy strings accepted ('true','1','yes' vs 'false','0','no','off').

query.description: Echo of the request parameters with defaults filled in.

AmountBYN.description: BYN monetary amount. May be a JSON number (when the controller casts to float) or a decimal string such as "424231.72" (when MariaDB ROUND(...,2) is passed through directly). Always parse as numeric.

Ratio.description: Conversion ratio in [0..1]. Null when the denominator is zero.

avg_rental_days.description: Average deal duration in days for this category (full deal, from start_date to return_date), averaged across rent_deals_act + rent_deals_arch for deals starting in the period. Null if no deals.

avg_first_rent_days.description: Average duration of the first-issuance sub-deal in days (sub-deal type IN first_rent, takeaway_plan). Computed from UNIX timestamps sd.to - sd.from, divided by 86400. Null if no first-rent sub-deals in period.

FinanceEntry.description: One row of the doh_rash income/expense ledger, in API shape (amount always a positive magnitude; direction carried by type1).

date.description: Accounting date (doh_rash.acc_date) — when the money moved, not when the record was created. This is the date all financial reports slice on.

amount.description: Positive magnitude in BYN. Direction (income vs. expense) is carried entirely by type1 — the API never returns a negative amount, even though doh_rash stores expenses as a negative number internally.

type1.description: Direction: rash = expense, doh = income. Rows with type1 outside this pair (shift_plus/shift_minus, paired till-transfer rows — about 39% of doh_rash) are never returned by this API: the list endpoint filters them out server-side and GET /finance/entries/{id} 404s for one. There is no parameter to include them. They exist to keep the physical till balance in sync, a single-row edit would desynchronize it, and in this API's shape they would be actively misleading — amount is always a positive magnitude, so a transfer row summed over a page would read as income, and their type2 belongs to neither dictionary so type2_name comes back null.

type2.description: Article code. Dictionary depends on type1: rash_items.ri_code for expenses, doh_items.rd_code for income.

type2_name.description: Human-readable label for type2, resolved from the matching dictionary. Resolves even for inactive/retired codes, so historical rows keep a readable label; null only if the code was removed from the dictionary entirely.

kassa.description: WHERE the money sits: k1/k2 = physical cash tills, card = card terminal, bank = bank account, safe = office safe. Paired with channel — see the channel × kassa rule in FinanceEntryInput.

channel.description: WHERE the transaction happened: an office number (as a string, e.g. "2"), "cur" (courier), "bank", or "safe" (office safe). Must pair validly with kassa (see FinanceEntryInput.channel description).

info.description: Free-text description of the transaction. Always non-empty.

dr_name_id.description: Which employee this entry is attributed to (logpass.logpass_id). 0 = not attributed to any employee. Required (non-zero) on write when type2 is zpl or avans (salary/advance) — that's what drives the legacy per-employee salary report.

link_to.description: Always 0 for rows this API can return or write. A non-zero link_to arms a cascade delete in the legacy admin (bb/doh-rash.php ships every row's delete form with dr_id_link = link_to, and deletes BOTH ids when it is > 0, with no type1 check), so writes through this API reject any non-zero value — see FinanceEntryInput.link_to. A non-zero value here can only be legacy data written outside this API.

created_at.description: Record creation time (doh_rash.cr_time), distinct from date/acc_date. Never used for report period filtering.

created_by_id.description: logpass_id of the row's creator (doh_rash.cr_who_id). For rows written through this API this is always the dedicated api_system logpass user — a client-supplied creator is never honored.

FinanceEntryInput.description: Write body for creating or patching a ledger entry. Every entry answers four questions: type1 (direction), type2 (article), channel (where it happened) and kassa (where the money sits). Only rows with type1 rash/doh can be written through this API — shift_plus/shift_minus (paired till-transfer rows) are out of scope by design, because a single-row write would desynchronize the physical till balance those pairs exist to keep in sync.

type1.description: Direction: "rash" = expense, "doh" = income. This is the only whitelist this write API accepts — shift_plus/shift_minus rows cannot be created, and an existing row whose type1 is outside {rash, doh} cannot be updated or deleted through this API at all.

type2.description: Article code, whose dictionary depends on type1. On write it must be an is_active=1 code: rash_items.ri_code when type1=rash, doh_items.rd_code when type1=doh. (On read, type2_name resolves the label even for inactive/retired codes, so old rows stay readable — but you cannot write a new row against a retired code.)

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Becomes the stored acc_date — the ACCOUNTING date (when the money moved), which is what every financial report slices on. This is distinct from created_at (record creation time), which the server sets and which you cannot supply.

amount.description: Positive magnitude in BYN, at most 2 decimal places (decimal(11,2) column). Always positive in both requests and responses — direction is carried by type1, not by the sign of amount. The server negates the value internally for storage when type1=rash; that sign-flip is an internal storage detail this API contract hides from callers.

kassa.description: WHERE the money sits after this transaction. Fixed whitelist: k1/k2 (physical cash tills), card (card terminal), bank (bank account), safe (office safe). Must form a valid pair with channel: kassa="bank" is only valid together with channel="bank"; kassa="safe" is only valid together with channel="safe" — the office safe is a channel of its own, cash that sits in the safe rather than in a till; bb/doh-rash.php moves money in and out of it only by a transfer between kassas. kassa in {k1, k2, card} requires channel to be a live office number or "cur" (courier). A mismatched pair (e.g. channel="bank" with kassa="k2") is rejected — money cannot be simultaneously in the bank account and a physical till.

channel.description: WHERE the transaction happened: an office number as a string (existence-gated against the offices table — a closed-but-existing office is still a valid channel, it need not be currently active), "cur" (courier), "bank", or "safe" (office safe). See kassa's description for the channel × kassa pairing rule this must satisfy.

info.description: Free-text description. Required and must be non-empty after trimming whitespace — this guards against silent TEXT-column truncation under this app's empty sql_mode. Max 2000 characters.

dr_name_id.description: Which employee this entry is attributed to (logpass.logpass_id). REQUIRED (and must reference an existing logpass row) when type2 is "zpl" or "avans" (salary/advance) — omitting it there silently breaks the legacy per-employee salary report. Optional otherwise, defaulting to 0 (not attributed to an employee); if supplied and non-zero it must still reference an existing logpass row.

link_to.description: MUST be 0 (the default). Any other value is rejected — do not loosen this without reading why. The legacy admin (bb/doh-rash.php) renders EVERY row's delete form with a hidden dr_id_link set to that row's link_to, and its delete handler runs DELETE FROM doh_rash WHERE dr_id IN ($dr_id, $dr_id_link) whenever that value is > 0 — with no type1 check, behind a confirm dialog that says "эту операцию" (singular). A rash/doh row carrying a non-zero link_to therefore silently destroys a second, unrelated row the next time a human deletes it in the admin, possibly one half of a shift_plus/shift_minus pair, corrupting a till balance. Rejecting only links that point AT a shift row would not close this: the legacy cascade deletes whatever dr_id it is handed. Linked/paired operations are out of scope for this API. Omitting the field (or sending null) is equivalent to 0.

FinanceEntryHistoryRow.description: One doh_rash_history journal row. Only 'update' and 'delete' actions are ever journalled — a newly created row is already self-describing via its own created_by/created_at, so inserts are not journalled.

dr_id.description: The doh_rash row this journal entry is about. For a delete, this id no longer exists in doh_rash — the journal is the only remaining record of it.

action.description: What happened. create is never journalled (see schema description).

before.description: Full snapshot of the doh_rash row's raw storage columns before the change (whole-row, not a diff). This is the recovery mechanism for a mistaken edit or delete — reconstruct the row from here.

after.description: Full snapshot of the row's raw storage columns after the change. Null for a delete action (there is no "after" row).

actor_user_id.description: logpass_id of who made the change. For changes made through this API, always the api_system logpass user.

source.description: Where the change came from, e.g. "mcp_api".

ip.description: Request IP that made the change.

created_at.description: When the journal row was written (not the accounting date of the underlying entry).

FinanceEntryBatchResultRow.description: Per-item outcome of a POST /finance/entries batch.

index.description: Position of this item in the submitted entries array.

status.description: Whether this specific item was written. One invalid item never blocks the others in the same batch.

dr_id.description: New row's primary key when status=created; null when status=invalid.

errors.description: field => message map when status=invalid; null when status=created.

OperationsFunnelData.description: May be `[]` (empty array) when category resolves to no razdel.

deals_by_source.description: Deal counts keyed by utm_source; 'direct' when no UTM attribution found.

office_type.description: 'office', 'courier', or null when offices row is missing.

period.description: Format depends on granularity, e.g. '2024-01' for month, '2024-W24' for week, '2024-Q2' for quarter, '2024' for year.

units_at_period_end.description: Historical unit count at period end (active items with buy_date<=ts, plus archived items still alive at ts). Null when the requested range spans more than 60 periods — see meta.warnings.

deals_per_unit.description: deals_started / units_at_period_end, rounded to 2 decimals. Null when units_at_period_end is null or 0.

InventoryFreeTreeData.description: Catalog tree: section → subsection → category → model.

total_units.description: Sum of free_units across all models in this category.

units_at_from.description: Historical unit count at period start (active + alive-archived).

units_at_to.description: Historical unit count at period end.

avg_rental_days_per_deal.description: Average deal duration per deal in days for this model (rented_days / deals_in_period). Zero if no deals.

avg_first_rent_days.description: Average duration of the initial issuance sub-deal in days (sub-deal type IN first_rent, takeaway_plan). Computed from sd.to - sd.from (UNIX seconds) / 86400. Null if the model had no first-rent sub-deals in the period.

last_deal_ts.description: Unix timestamp of the last deal touching this model. Null = never.

PricingHistoryRow.description: One event from rent_tarif_history. Each event stores a full before/after snapshot of the tariff row, not a diff.

source.description: Writer of the event: an edit in the legacy admin panel, tariff removal on model archival, the one-off migration that seeded the table from the then-live rent_tarif_act (change_type=baseline), or the legacy rent_tarif_prev import (always change_type=delete).

before.description: Tariff state before the change. Null when change_type is create or baseline.

step.description: Empty string / null are legacy junk, not a documented step: 3 rows in rent_tarif_prev (tarif_act_id 35, 39, 8157; model_id=0) were imported with an empty step by migration 2026_07_31_000001 (source=legacy_import). bb/classes/TariffHistory::quote() also collapses an empty string to SQL NULL, so both forms can appear.

price_per_day.description: rent_amount / (step_days × kol_vo), 2 decimals. Null when that denominator is zero.

after.description: Tariff state after the change. Null when change_type is delete.

step.description: Empty string / null are legacy junk, not a documented step: 3 rows in rent_tarif_prev (tarif_act_id 35, 39, 8157; model_id=0) were imported with an empty step by migration 2026_07_31_000001 (source=legacy_import). bb/classes/TariffHistory::quote() also collapses an empty string to SQL NULL, so both forms can appear.

price_per_day.description: rent_amount / (step_days × kol_vo), 2 decimals. Null when that denominator is zero.

delta_amount_byn.description: after.rent_amount − before.rent_amount, formatted to 2 decimals. Null unless both before and after are present.

delta_pct.description: Percent change in price_per_day: (after.price_per_day − before.price_per_day) / before.price_per_day × 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Null unless both sides have a price_per_day and before.price_per_day > 0.

PricingSnapshotRow.description: One model's price list as of `as_of`: the latest rent_tarif_history event with changed_at <= as_of, per tarif_id.

extrapolated.description: True if at least one of this model's tariff rows has no recorded change-log event before as_of, so its baseline record (state as of its own last known edit) is returned instead — see meta.warnings.

step.description: Empty string / null are legacy junk, not a documented step: 3 rows in rent_tarif_prev (tarif_act_id 35, 39, 8157; model_id=0) were imported with an empty step by migration 2026_07_31_000001 (source=legacy_import). bb/classes/TariffHistory::quote() also collapses an empty string to SQL NULL, so both forms can appear.

price_per_day.description: rent_amount / (step_days × kol_vo), 2 decimals. Null when that denominator is zero.

unique_clients_proxy.description: DISTINCT deal_id of issuance sub-deals — proxy for unique customers visiting that office in that period.

avg_payment_byn.description: Average sub-deal payment (NOT average per deal).

first_activity_date.description: Earliest sub_deal.acc_date for this office. Renamed from first_deal_date in v2.0.0.

last_activity_date.description: Latest sub_deal.acc_date for this office. Renamed from last_deal_date in v2.0.0.

seasonality_index.description: deals / (totalDeals / monthsObserved). 1.0 = average month; 6.7 = December for costumes.

total_revenue_byn.description: Pre-aggregated per item to avoid M:N inflation through subrazdel_category × razdel_subrazdel.

MarketingConversionRow.description: A single conversion event from tiktak_utms with UTM attribution and entity details.

entity_type.description: Conversion type. zvonki=callback request; rent_orders=online booking (standard items); karn_brons=carnival costume booking; kb_zayavki=waitlist request (out-of-stock); phone_click/add_to_cart_click=JS frontend events (entity_id=0, fio/phone/status=null).

fio.description: Customer name from joined entity. CONCAT_WS(' ', family, name, otch) for rent_orders; fio for karn_brons; z_name for zvonki. Null for frontend click events.

phone.description: Customer phone from joined entity. Null for frontend click events.

info.description: Free-text info from joined entity (zvonki.info or kb_zayavki.info). Null for others.

status.description: Entity status (zvonki.status, rent_orders.status, karn_brons.status). Null for kb_zayavki and click events.

model_id.description: Model ID for rent_orders (from rent_orders.model_id) and kb_zayavki (from kb_zayavki.model_id). Null for all other entity types.

model_name.description: Human-readable model name from rent_model_web.item_name_main. Populated for rent_orders and kb_zayavki. Null for all other entity types.

cat_id.description: Category ID from rent_orders.cat_id. Only populated for rent_orders. Null for all other entity types (including kb_zayavki, where cat_id is not stored).

cat_name.description: Category name from tovar_rent_cat.rent_cat_name. Only populated for rent_orders. Null for all other entity types.

PagesProductRow.description: One L3 product page. `current_values`/`default_values` are present only with fields=full.

full_url.description: Canonical path, resolved through tovar_rent_cat.main_sub_razdel_id → sub_razdel.main_razdel_id (the chain the site uses for <link rel=canonical> and sitemap.xml). null when the category is not wired into the catalog tree — the page then has no URL at all.

active_units.description: Rows in tovar_rent_items for this model.

is_indexable.description: status=show AND canonical URL exists AND active_units>0 — the same rule sitemap.xml applies.

current_values.description: Current stored values; null means the field is empty.

h1.description: rent_model_web.item_name_main — the <h1> of the product page.

main_pic_title.description: title= attribute of the main image (m_a_title).

faq.description: FAQ entries rendered as FAQPage schema.org markup.

default_values.description: Current stored values; null means the field is empty.

h1.description: rent_model_web.item_name_main — the <h1> of the product page.

main_pic_title.description: title= attribute of the main image (m_a_title).

faq.description: FAQ entries rendered as FAQPage schema.org markup.

PagesProductInput.description: Partial update. Only the keys present are written. meta_title/meta_description/*_alt/main_pic_title/breadcrumb_name are stripped of well-formed tags and of the characters " < > (they land inside <title> or an HTML attribute); description and h1 keep their markup. Values headed for a TEXT column (description, faq) are rejected with 422 above 60000 bytes — production runs with an empty sql_mode, so MySQL would truncate them silently.

h1.description: Product page <h1> (item_name_main). May be edited but not blanked — it is the product name in the admin panel and printed forms too.

l2_name.description: Card title on listing pages. May be edited but not blanked.

description.description: Body copy (HTML). Not sanitised. Max 60000 bytes.

faq.description: FAQ entries rendered as FAQPage schema.org markup.

field.description: API field name, not the DB column.

FinanceEntryDeleteResponse.description: Confirmation of physical deletion. Recovery is via GET /finance/entries/history, not a status flag — the row is actually removed from doh_rash.

FinanceEntryBatchEnvelope.description: Per-item outcome of a batch create. HTTP 200 even when some items are invalid — only whole-request shape problems (empty array, >200 items) are HTTP 422.

FinanceEntryHistoryEnvelope.description: Paginated change journal (update/delete only) for the ledger.

FinanceEntryNotEditable.description: This entry's type1 is outside {rash, doh} (a shift_plus/shift_minus till-transfer row) and cannot be written through this API.

RedirectSingleResponse.description: A single redirect record (create / update result).

PagesProductListEnvelope.description: Paginated list of L3 product pages with SEO completeness counters.

PagesProductSingleEnvelope.description: One L3 product page with its current and default SEO values.

PagesProductBulkEnvelope.description: Per-item outcome of a bulk SEO update.

PagesHistoryEnvelope.description: Field-level change log of SEO content written through this API.

SlugConflict.description: The slug maps to more than one rent_model_web row; reading or writing it would be ambiguous.

get.summary: Liveness probe (no DB).
Returns this OpenAPI spec.

200.description: OpenAPI document.

get.summary: Business categories + detailed tovar_cats list.
Offices/couriers with computed first/last deal + revenue.
Active rash_items dictionary.
Active doh_items dictionary.
Latest write timestamp per hot table + global max.
Revenue (total + non-carnival + carnival), expenses (7 buckets), EBITDA. Adds 2025 bank-channel warning when range overlaps 2025+.
Rental revenue from UNION(sub_deals_act, sub_deals_arch) by acc_date.
Rental revenue and duration by category.
doh_rash expenses by period × type2 × channel.
Inflow/outflow/net per till (kassa).
List ledger entries (filtered, paginated).
get.description: Reads the doh_rash income/expense ledger directly (not a period aggregation — see /finance/expenses and /finance/revenue for those). Ordered acc_date DESC, dr_id DESC. Only rash/doh rows are ever returned — shift_plus/shift_minus till-transfer rows are excluded server-side and cannot be opted back in (see FinanceEntry.type1). A reversed range (to earlier than from) is rejected with a 422 rather than returning an empty page: on a finance endpoint, "nothing happened in this period" and "you swapped your dates" must not look identical.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Filter acc_date >= this date (inclusive). No default — omit for no lower bound.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Filter acc_date <= this date (inclusive). No default — omit for no upper bound. Must not be earlier than `from` — a reversed range is a 422, not an empty result set.

post.description: Accepts 1-200 entries per request. Each item is validated and written independently — one invalid item never blocks the others, so the overall response is HTTP 200 with a per-item status; only whole-request shape problems (empty array, more than 200 items) are HTTP 422. Only type1 rash/doh may be created — shift_plus/shift_minus rows are out of scope. Server always sets created_by/created_at (api_system logpass user, current time); any client-supplied value for these is silently ignored. Creates are never journalled to doh_rash_history — a new row is already self-describing via its own created_by/created_at. Per-item validation enforces the channel × kassa pairing (kassa="bank" only with channel="bank"; kassa="safe" only with channel="safe"; kassa in {k1, k2, card} requires channel to be a live office number or "cur") and requires dr_name_id, referencing an existing logpass row, when type2 is "zpl" or "avans". link_to must be 0 on every item — see FinanceEntryInput.link_to.

get.summary: Read a single ledger entry.
get.description: A shift_plus/shift_minus id returns the same 404 as an unknown id — from this API's perspective there is no entry with that id (see FinanceEntry.type1).

patch.description: Validation runs against the MERGED row (existing columns with the submitted patch fields applied on top), not just the submitted body — a field you don't touch can still fail if it no longer pairs with a field you did patch (e.g. patching only kassa on a row whose existing channel doesn't pair with the new kassa), or simply because the STORED value was already invalid under this API's stricter write rules. Two rules apply to that merged row specifically: channel and kassa must form a valid pair (kassa="bank" only with channel="bank"; kassa="safe" only with channel="safe"; kassa in {k1, k2, card} requires channel to be a live office number or "cur"), and dr_name_id — referencing an existing logpass row — is required when type2 is "zpl" or "avans". Two merged-row failures are commonly inherited rather than caused by the caller, and their messages say so: `info` (about 20% of existing rash/doh rows have an empty info — legacy data predating this API; supply info with your patch to fix the row) and `link_to` (a legacy row carrying a non-zero link_to cannot be patched until you send link_to: 0 — see FinanceEntryInput.link_to for why non-zero is refused at all). The patch is read from the JSON request BODY only: query-string parameters are never treated as patch fields, and a body containing no patchable field at all (empty, or only unknown keys) is a 422 rather than a no-op that rewrites the row with its own values. Refuses (422) when the EXISTING row's type1 is outside {rash, doh} — a shift_plus/shift_minus row can never be retyped or edited through this API. A successful update is journalled to doh_rash_history with a full before/after row snapshot, best-effort: a journal-write failure is logged (with the full payload) but never rolls back the doh_rash write that already succeeded, so a 200 means the ledger row changed and is not by itself a guarantee that a history row exists for it.

schema.description: Any subset of these fields, sent in the JSON request body (query-string parameters are ignored). At least one of these fields must be present — a body of only unknown keys is a 422. Same field semantics as FinanceEntryInput; see that schema for what each field means.

type2.description: Article code. See FinanceEntryInput.type2 — must be an is_active code in the dictionary matching the (possibly patched) type1.

kassa.description: Where the money sits. Must pair validly with the (possibly patched) channel — see FinanceEntryInput.kassa.

channel.description: Where it happened. Must pair validly with the (possibly patched) kassa — see FinanceEntryInput.channel.

dr_name_id.description: Attributed employee. Required for type2 zpl/avans (using the merged, i.e. possibly-patched, type2) — see FinanceEntryInput.dr_name_id.

link_to.description: Must be 0. See FinanceEntryInput.link_to — and note a legacy row that already holds a non-zero link_to can only be patched by sending link_to: 0 to clear it. Omitting the field (or sending null) is equivalent to 0.

422.description: Either the merged row failed field validation, or the existing row is not editable through this API (see FinanceEntryNotEditable).

delete.description: This is a hard delete — the row is actually removed from doh_rash, there is no soft-delete flag. Recovery is via GET /finance/entries/history (the before snapshot journalled at delete time), not a status flag. Refuses (422) when the row's type1 is outside {rash, doh} — deleting one half of a shift_plus/shift_minus pair would leave the other half dangling and the till balance wrong. The journal actor is resolved BEFORE the row is touched, so a delete that could not be journalled fails with a 500 and leaves the row intact rather than becoming unrecoverable; the journal INSERT itself is still best-effort (a failure is logged with the full row snapshot, never rolled back).

500.description: Delete aborted because the journal actor could not be resolved — an unjournalled delete would be unrecoverable, so the row is left intact.

get.summary: Read the change journal (doh_rash_history) — update/delete only.
get.description: Records only 'update' and 'delete' actions with a full before/after row snapshot; 'create' is never journalled because a newly created row is already self-describing via its own created_by/created_at. This is the recovery mechanism for a mistaken PATCH or DELETE made through this API. A reversed range (to earlier than from) is rejected with a 422 rather than returning an empty page.

parameters.name: dr_id
parameters.description: Filter to journal rows about this doh_rash entry (works even after the entry itself has been deleted).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Filter journal created_at <= this date. Must not be earlier than `from` — a reversed range is a 422, not an empty result set.

get.summary: Lead → deal → sub-deal → return funnel with conversion rates. issuance_events = sub_deal type IN first_rent/takeaway_plan (matches /bb/reports.php deal counts).
Period-bucketed funnel.
Per-razdel orders + deals + revenue. Revenue is pre-aggregated per item to avoid M:N inflation.
Per-office deals + revenue + issuance_events + renewal_events. office_id=0 is the synthetic 'Курьер' row (delivery_yn='1' sub-deals).
New deals started per model per period, with units_at_period_end (historical inventory denominator) and deals_per_unit as a turnover proxy.
Current catalog tree with free-unit counts.
Current active catalog models pricing with calculated daily rate.
Per-physical-item profitability across UNION(deals_act, deals_arch).

Per-model utilization = rented_seconds / (avg_units × period). Also returns avg_rental_days_per_deal (total rented days / deals) and avg_first_rent_days (avg duration of first-issuance sub-deals, type IN first_rent/takeaway_plan). Historical inventory at date = active items (buy_date<=ts) + archived items still alive (buy_date<=ts AND arch_time>=ts).
Per-model turnover = deals / units.
Models without rentals for at least N days.

Change log of tariff edits from rent_tarif_history. Each event carries a full before/after snapshot of the tariff row, not a diff — reconstructing the price list on an arbitrary date means taking, per tarif_id, the latest event with changed_at <= that date (see /pricing/snapshot, which does exactly that).

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on changed_at. Default: no lower bound.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on changed_at. Default: no upper bound.

parameters.name: change_type

get.summary: Price list reconstructed as of `as_of`: for each tarif_id, the latest rent_tarif_history event with changed_at <= as_of (deleted tariffs excluded). A tariff row with no recorded event before as_of, but already effective on that date (new_start_date <= as_of), is still returned — with extrapolated=true — using its baseline snapshot (the state as of its own earliest known edit, dated anywhere from 2013 to today); this share shrinks as more real events accumulate. See meta.warnings for the extrapolated-row count on a given response.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Reconstruct the price list as of this date (inclusive, end of day).

Distribution of intervals between consecutive deals (mean/p25/median/p75/histogram).
Per-client LTV ranking across UNION(deals_act, deals_arch). No PII.
Distinct clients × deals × revenue by trimmed/lower-cased city.

Per-period × per-office revenue, deals, issuance_events. Office attribution via sub_deal.place + delivery_yn (per-payment). office_id=0 is the Курьер pseudo-office. avg_payment_byn is per sub-deal payment, not per deal.
Office full lifecycle: first/last activity date (sub_deal.acc_date), total revenue, currently_active flag.
Monthly seasonality_index for a business category over the last N years.
Per-category deals + revenue + active models. Revenue pre-aggregated per item to avoid M:N inflation. Requires date_from + date_to (NOT from/to).
Carnival booking funnel: bookings → approved → issued → returned. Source: karn_brons + karn_brons_arch (separate from regular rentals).
Monthly carnival seasonality_index. December is the peak.

Per-period carnival revenue by payment channel (k1/k2/terminal/bank). NOTE: this is the karn_brons pre-booking system — separate from /finance/revenue which sums rent_sub_deals. DO NOT sum both — that double-counts carnival revenue.
Streaming CSV export. Topics: operations, revenue, pnl, traffic. Column layout matches data/monthly/_schema.md.
